🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Rochelle Fleming, the founding lead singer of the Philadelphia soul and disco group First Choice, has died at 72.

Fleming died on Wednesday, November 5, 2026, in Philadelphia. Her death was announced on Friday, November 7, by her manager, George “Iz” Correia, on her official Facebook page and in a memorial message on her Instagram account, on behalf of the Fleming/Finney family. “She brought light, laughter and love to the world,” Correia wrote. No cause of death has been publicly disclosed.

Born in Philadelphia, Fleming began singing as a teenager at Overbrook High School with classmates Annette Guest and Wardell Piper in a group called the Debonettes. Discovered by radio personality Georgie Woods, the group became First Choice, and Fleming’s powerful lead voice carried them to the top of the charts.

Their 1973 breakthrough, “Armed and Extremely Dangerous,” reached No. 11 on the R&B chart and No. 28 on the Billboard Hot 100, and climbed into the U.K. Top 20. It was followed by “Smarty Pants,” “Doctor Love” and “Love Thang.” In 1983, “Let No Man Put Asunder” became the group’s signature song, reaching No. 13 on the Billboard dance chart and going on to become a cornerstone of Chicago house music, sampled and played on dance floors around the world for decades.

Fleming continued to record and perform internationally as a solo artist, and in 2014 she reunited with her First Choice bandmates for a celebrated concert at New York’s East River Bandshell. In 2019, J. Cole introduced First Choice to a new generation when he sampled their song “Wake Up to Me” on his hit “Middle Child.” Her passing came just a week after the release of “Anywhere,” a long-unreleased song by her former groupmate Wardell Piper.

Rest in Peace, Rochelle Fleming.

Sources: SoulTracks, reporting the announcement by her manager George “Iz” Correia on behalf of the Fleming/Finney family; That Eric Alper; Soundee.
